_doc: Who asks whom (owner-only; scripts/route.sh reads it, wake-agents fires the routines). Names are labels: change a role's `name`, `avatar` or `app` here (the live GitHub App slug, used for the git identity) and in the App settings, nothing else. A role's logins are its GitHub accounts, old and new while an App is being renamed; while agent identities are paused, agents post as the owner and a `<!-- role: x -->` marker names the role. A channel is an issue label. from/to: who may open it and who is woken; on_reply: who is woken when the owner comments; on_close: who is woken when it closes. A debate channel alternates between two roles, each gets at most `turns` turns, then `escalate_to` takes it to the owner. on_reply/on_close "raiser" means the role in the issue body's `<!-- raised-by: x -->` marker, else the role of the issue's author, else the lead. Each worker handles its own PRs: a finished merge review or failed CI on a PR wakes the worker or lead whose login opened it, else default_worker (owner PRs); red main wakes the lead. mentions: an owner comment containing one of these handles wakes exactly those roles, on any issue or PR; so does a comment by the research bot (Ada), which is how her answers reach the PM, lead and workers. The @locksmith-hq/<name> handles are muted org teams (no notifications) that exist only so the handles autocomplete; a new one needs its team too. Add a role or channel here, plus its secret in wake-agents.yml.
